nl.statement: A fixed-dimension linear Gaussian covariance-shift structural causal model observed across environments. The observed dimension is \(d\ge 2\), the environment labels are \(\mathcal E=\{0,1,\ldots,E\}\) with \(E\ge 2\) nonbaseline environments, the observed labels are \(\mathcal V=\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and the target size is \(r\in\{1,\ldots,d-1\}\). A model \(\mu\) consists of an observed structural coefficient matrix \(B_{\mu}\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}\) that is permutation-similar to a strictly lower-triangular matrix, with total-effect matrix \(U_{\mu}=(I_d-B_{\mu})^{-1}\); an invariant latent loading \(C_{\mu}\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}\) with invariant latent covariance \(\Omega_{H,\mu}\succeq 0\); a strictly positive baseline structural-noise variance vector \(\omega_{0,\mu}\in\mathbb R^d\); an invariant diagonal measurement-error covariance \(\Omega_{\eta,\mu}\succ 0\); a target set \(T_{\mu}\subseteq\mathcal V\) of size \(r\); and variance increments \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^{E\times d}\) with \(\lambda_0=0\), vanishing off \(T_{\mu}\), nonnegative on \(T_{\mu}\), and strictly positive for each target in at least one nonbaseline environment. In environment \(e\) the primitive vector \((H_e,\varepsilon_e,\eta_e)\) is centered Gaussian with mutually independent blocks and coordinates, \(\operatorname{Cov}(H_e)=\Omega_{H,\mu}\), \(\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_e)=\operatorname{diag}(\omega_{0,\mu}+\lambda_e)\), and \(\operatorname{Cov}(\eta_e)=\Omega_{\eta,\mu}\), and the observation is \(Y_e=U_{\mu}(C_{\mu}H_e+\varepsilon_e)+\eta_e\). The legal class \(\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\) collects all such \(\mu\). — Search trace: grepped `../doc/API.md` section index (`^## `) and then grepped the whole index for `Wishart|empirical covariance|sample covariance` (0 hits) and read sections 17b (`Discovery/LinearDisentanglement/`, lines 11638-11760) and 9b/9-9l (`SCM/ID/`, `PO/ID/Exact/`); globbed `../Causalean/Discovery/LinearDisentanglement/**` and `../Causalean/Mathlib/**`; Mathlib checked with `lean_loogle "IsGaussian"` and `lean_leansearch "mutually independent family of random variables iIndepFun"`. Result: no Causalean world models a multi-environment linear-Gaussian SCM with invariant latent confounding PLUS invariant measurement error PLUS per-environment structural-variance shifts. Two near misses, both at the wrong abstraction: (a) `Causalean.Discovery.LinearDisentanglement.Solution` (`Causalean/Discovery/LinearDisentanglement/Model.lean`) is a latent SEM with a full-row-rank mixing and ONE perfect single-node intervention per context, indexed by precision matrices, with no additive measurement error and no nonnegative-shift design; (b) the sibling CausalSmith note `CausalSmith.ExactID.RobustBackshiftUniformDistance.BackshiftSystem` (`CausalSmith/ExactID/EID_RobustBackshiftUniformDistance_Research/Basic.lean:42`) is the closest sibling record but permits cyclic coefficients, carries no latent loading and no measurement error, and its shifts are the whole model rather than an exact-rank target fiber. Both are recorded as STYLE references for F2 (matrix/environment abbreviations, `@realizes` annotation discipline) rather than reuse. Cluster-root modules `Causalean/PO/**`, `Causalean/SCM/ID/**`, `Causalean/SCM/Do/**`, `Causalean/Graph/SWIG.lean` are bypass-justified per decision P7. Reused pieces INSIDE the world: `Matrix.BlockTriangular` (verified `lean_loogle Matrix.BlockTriangular`, module `Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Block`) for acyclicity, `Matrix.PosDef`/`Matrix.PosSemidef` for the covariance cones, `ProbabilityTheory.IsGaussian` and `ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun` for the primitive-law assumptions, `Causalean.Mathlib.stdGaussian` for the standard-Gaussian building block used by the realization construction.

The observable covariance-tuple and ordered-certificate world. A population covariance tuple is \(\theta=(\Sigma_0,\ldots,\Sigma_E)\) with \(\Sigma_e\) real symmetric \(d\times d\); the covariance shifts are \(\Delta_e=\Sigma_e-\Sigma_0\) with \(\Delta_0=0\), and the aggregate carrier is \(\bar Q=\sum_{e=1}^E\Delta_e\). For a candidate label set \(T\subseteq\mathcal V\) and an ordering \(t=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\) of \(T\), the selection matrix \(P_t\in\{0,1\}^{r\times d}\) picks the coordinates in the order \(t\), the ordered aggregate principal block is \(\bar Q_{tt}=P_t\bar QP_t^{\mathsf T}\), and when \(\bar Q_{tt}\succ0\) it has the unique factorization \(\bar Q_{tt}=L_tD_tL_t^{\mathsf T}\) with \(L_t\) unit lower triangular and \(D_t\) diagonal positive, giving the transformed target blocks \(\Lambda_{e,t}=L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}\). The reconstruction map is \(W_t=\bar QP_t^{\mathsf T}\bar Q_{tt}^{-1}\), the recovered target columns are \(A_t=W_tL_t\), and the completion places \(t\) first to form the unit-lower-triangular \(U_t\), the structural matrix \(B_t=I_d-U_t^{-1}\), the slack \(\tau>0\), the baseline remainder \(R_0=\Sigma_0-\tau U_tU_t^{\mathsf T}-\tau I_d\), and the loading \(C_t=U_t^{-1}R_0^{1/2}\). Over this world sit the causal fiber \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)\), the algebraic fiber \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{LDL}}(\theta)\), the compulsory and possible label sets \(\mathcal C(\theta)\) and \(\mathcal P(\theta)\) with \(h(\theta)=(\mathcal C(\theta),\mathcal P(\theta))\), and the subset-memoized pivot state \((R_S,(M_{e,S})_{e=1}^E)\) indexed by selected subsets \(S\subseteq\mathcal V\) with \(|S|\le r\). Three explicit tuples live here: the three-node signed-shift witness \(\theta^{\pm}\), the three-node split-reference witness \(\theta^{\mathrm{split}}\), and the four-node collision path \(\theta_{\gamma}\) indexed by \(\gamma\in(-1,1)\). — Search trace: grepped `../doc/API.md` for `Cholesky|LDL` and read section 10j' (line 5707); grepped `../Causalean/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Cholesky.lean` for `^(theorem|lemma|def|namespace)` (confirms `Causalean.Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.{ldl_lowerInv_diag_one, ldl_diagEntries_pos, ldl_lowerInv_blockTriangular, ldl_lower_blockTriangular, ldl_lower_diag_one, cholesky_exists, orthogonal_upperTri_pos_diag_eq_one, cholesky_unique}`); Mathlib checked with `lean_loogle LDL.lower_conj_diag` (hit: `LDL.lower hS * LDL.diag hS * (LDL.lower hS)^H = S`, module `Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.LDL`), `lean_leansearch "positive semidefinite matrix has a positive semidefinite square root"` (hit: `Matrix.PosSemidef.sqrt`, `Matrix.PosSemidef.sq_sqrt`, module `Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Order`), `lean_leansearch "rank of a matrix over a field"` (hit: `Matrix.rank`, module `Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.Rank`). Result: the positive `LDL^T` factorization with unit-lower factor is EXACTLY Mathlib's `LDL.lower`/`LDL.diag` plus `LDL.lower_conj_diag`, and its uniqueness (the step `thm:sharp-target-fiber` spends a paragraph on) follows from `Causalean.Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.cholesky_unique` after absorbing the square roots of the diagonal factor, exactly the direction `cholesky_exists` already travels. The unit-diagonal and positive-pivot side facts `ldl_lower_diag_one` and `ldl_diagEntries_pos` are also direct reuse. `R_0^{1/2}` is `Matrix.PosSemidef.sqrt`. What is NOT in the library and is built here: the ordered SELECTION operator \(P_t\), the ordered principal-block certificate, the two fibers, the completion, and the subset pivot state. `lean_local_search` was tried first for all four Cholesky names and returned empty for every one — treated as tool flakiness, not absence, and confirmed by direct source grep.

The bounded multi-sample Gaussian covariance experiment. Constants \(0<m<M\) bound the spectrum, and \(\Theta_K\) is the class of tuples \(\zeta=(Z_0,\ldots,Z_E)\) of positive-definite matrices with \(mI_d\preceq Z_e\preceq MI_d\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\), aggregate difference \(\sum_{f=1}^E(Z_f-Z_0)\) of rank exactly \(r\), every \(\operatorname{range}(Z_e-Z_0)\) contained in the range of that aggregate, and at least one ordered certificate. Given sample sizes \(n=(n_0,\ldots,n_E)\), the observations \(Y_{ei}\sim N(0,\Sigma_e)\) are independent over \(e\in\mathcal E\) and \(1\le i\le n_e\), with empirical covariances \(\widehat\Sigma_e=n_e^{-1}\sum_{i}Y_{ei}Y_{ei}^{\mathsf T}\). The tuple space carries the sample-size weighted Frobenius norm \(\lVert a\rVert_w^2=\sum_{e=0}^En_e\lVert a_e\rVert_F^2\) and, at a fixed \(\theta\), the frozen Gaussian covariance-information norm \(\lVert H\rVert_{I,n,\theta}^2=\tfrac12\sum_{e=0}^{E}n_e\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma_e^{-1}H_e\Sigma_e^{-1}H_e)\). At level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\) with \(V_{\max}=(E+1)M^2d(d+1)\) and \(c_{\alpha}=\sqrt{V_{\max}/\alpha}\), the raw region is \(W_n=\{\zeta:mI_d\preceq Z_e\preceq MI_d,\ \lVert\zeta-\widehat\Sigma\rVert_w\le c_{\alpha}\}\); for tolerance \(\epsilon>0\) the strict approximate-minimizer graph is \(G_{\epsilon}=\{(s,\zeta):\zeta\in\Theta_K,\ \lVert\zeta-s\rVert_w<\inf_{\xi\in\Theta_K}\lVert\xi-s\rVert_w+\epsilon\}\), a certified selector \(s_{\epsilon}\) is a section of it, \(\widetilde\theta_n=s_1(\widehat\Sigma)\), and \(R_n=W_n\cup\{\widetilde\theta_n\}\) carries the outer family \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{out},n}\) and the classification image \(\mathcal H_n\). The classification information distance is \(\delta_n(\theta)=\inf\{\lVert\zeta-\theta\rVert_{I,n,\theta}:\zeta\in\Theta_K,\ h(\zeta)\ne h(\theta)\}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=\infty\); \(C<\infty\) bounds it in the impossibility regime and \(x>0\) is the deterministic sampling-error threshold. — Search trace: grepped `../doc/API.md` for `Wishart|empirical covariance|sample covariance` (0 hits) and for `Isserlis|Chebyshev|two-point|Le Cam|chiSq|Hellinger|totalVariation` (hits at 7390-7474, `Stat/Minimax/`); read sections 12w.1-12w.3; grepped `../Causalean/Stat/Minimax/TotalVariation.lean` (`namespace Causalean.Stat`, `tvDist` at :50, `one_sub_tvDist_le_test` at :108); grepped `../Causalean/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/CompactArgminSelection.lean` (`namespace Causalean.Mathlib.MeasureTheory`, `borelMeasurable_compact_argmin_selector` at :134, `borelMeasurable_nearestPoint_selector` at :338). Result: Causalean has NO empirical-covariance / Wishart second-moment layer, so the fourth-moment identity behind \(\mathbb E\lVert\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\rVert_F^2=n^{-1}\{(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma)^2+\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma^2)\}\) is built inline in `Helpers/Sampling.lean`. It DOES have the testing core the impossibility theorem needs (`Causalean.Stat.tvDist`, `Causalean.Stat.one_sub_tvDist_le_test`, the Le Cam and Pinsker layers), recorded as a reference and not a discharge (the testing bound is stated for total variation over a two-point pair while the paper's bound is a Holder argument on a \(p\)-th likelihood-ratio moment). ROUND-2 CORRECTION: the measurable-selection modules of `Causalean/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/` are NO LONGER on the route for this world. `borelMeasurable_compact_argmin_selector` requires `IsCompact K`, and \(\Theta_K\) is neither closed nor open (exact rank plus strict pivots), so it does not apply; it also delivers only Borel measurability, which is weaker than the semialgebraic section the core states. The selector is instead built from a FINITE net of \(\Theta_K\) (bounded by the Loewner box, hence totally bounded: `ProperSpace.isCompact_closedBall` in `Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.ProperSpace`, `IsCompact.totallyBounded` and `TotallyBounded.subset` and `totallyBounded_iff_subset` in `Mathlib.Topology.UniformSpace.Cauchy`, the last of which returns a net whose centres lie IN the set — verified round 2 by `lean_loogle "totallyBounded_iff_subset"` and `lean_leansearch "subset of a totally bounded set is totally bounded"`), which makes the section piecewise constant on finitely many polynomial cells and therefore both semialgebraic and Borel. See decisions P2, P3, P8.

The Gaussian local tangent experiment attached to a collision. A tangent geometry is a triple \(\mathcal G=(k,g_0,\mathcal A)\) with \(k\) the whitened local dimension, \(X\sim N(g,I_k)\) the local Gaussian shift experiment, \(g_0\in\mathbb R^k\) the focal shift carrying the focal complete classification, and \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R^k\) the union of tangent sets carrying a different complete classification. A randomized certification rule is a Borel \(\phi:\mathbb R^k\to[0,1]\); it is honest at level \(\alpha\) when \(\sup_{g\in\mathcal A}\mathbb E_g\phi(X)\le\alpha\), and the geometry-indexed optimal focal-certification value is \(\beta^{\star}_{\mathcal G}(\alpha)=\sup\{\mathbb E_{g_0}\phi(X):\phi\text{ honest at }\alpha\}\). The nearest-opposite distance \(c=\inf_{g\in\mathcal A}\lVert g-g_0\rVert_2\) is retained as a scalar summary of the geometry. — Search trace: grepped `../doc/API.md` for `Neyman|NeymanPearson|likelihood ratio test` (hits only at 3587-3613, the Dorn-Guo MSM quantile-balancing exchange argument, and at 5863/6594/9372-9385, Neyman ORTHOGONALITY, a different notion) and read section 10a''' (line 4368); grepped `../Causalean/Mathlib/Probability/StdNormalCDF.lean` (`namespace Causalean.Mathlib`, `stdNormalPDF` :40, `stdNormalCDF` :47, `stdNormalCDF_neg` :84, `stdNormalCDF_continuous` :117, `stdNormalCDF_strictMono` :123, `probit` :164, `stdNormalCDF_probit` :167, `probit_stdNormalCDF` :194); Mathlib checked with `lean_loogle "IsGaussian"` (module `Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Basic`, plus `gaussianReal`). Result: Mathlib and Causalean have NO general Neyman-Pearson lemma, so the one-sided and two-sided optimality exchange arguments are built inline (the frozen proof already supplies self-contained signed-integrand arguments). The scalar layer is exact reuse: `Causalean.Mathlib.stdNormalCDF` is \(\Phi\), `Causalean.Mathlib.probit` is \(\Phi^{-1}\), `stdNormalCDF_probit` gives \(\Phi(\Phi^{-1}(\alpha))=\alpha\), `stdNormalCDF_strictMono` and `stdNormalCDF_continuous` give the unique root \(t_{c,\alpha}\) of \(\Phi(t-c)-\Phi(-t-c)=\alpha\), and `stdNormalCDF_neg` gives the reflection identity. The nearest ANALOGOUS proved exchange argument, recorded for F3 to adapt, is `Causalean/PO/ID/Partial/Sensitivity/MSM/QuantileBalance.lean` `cutoff_optimal` / `cutoff_optimal_lower` (`../doc/API.md:3592`, :3613): same signed-integrand structure (integrand times a sign-controlled weight difference, the level term cancelling by calibration), applied there to a cutoff weight rather than to a likelihood-ratio test region. Gap to bridge: our reference measure in the two-sided case is the mixture \(Q=(P_c+P_{-c})/2\), so the exchange must be run after reflection symmetrization.
The observed coefficient matrix \(B_{\mu}\) is permutation-similar to a strictly lower-triangular matrix.

review.note: Matrix.BlockTriangular id makes the permuted matrix upper triangular and the second conjunct zeros its diagonal; existentially reversing the finite ordering gives exactly permutation-similarity to a strictly lower-triangular matrix, and conversely.

standard.name: Acyclic linear structural equation model
standard.citation: Yang, Yuqin, Saber Salehkaleybar, and Negar Kiyavash. 2024. ``Learning Unknown Intervention Targets in Structural Causal Models from Heterogeneous Data.'' Proceedings of AISTATS, PMLR 238:3187--3195. arXiv:2312.06091.

nl.statement: For every \(e\in\mathcal E\), the primitive vector \((H_e,\varepsilon_e,\eta_e)\) is centered Gaussian.

review.note: IsGaussian specifies a Gaussian law for the complete primitive vector, and the coordinatewise integral equalities specify its zero mean, exactly expressing centered joint Gaussianity.

standard.name: Linear Gaussian latent-variable model
standard.citation: Varici, Burak, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Prasanna Sattigeri, and Ali Tajer. 2022. ``Intervention Target Estimation in the Presence of Latent Variables.'' Proceedings of UAI, PMLR 180:2013--2023.

nl.statement: For every \(e\in\mathcal E\), the collection consisting of \(H_e\), all coordinates of \(\varepsilon_e\), and \(\eta_e\) is mutually independent.

review.note: The heterogeneous iIndepFun family consists exactly of the whole latent block, every individual structural-noise coordinate, and the whole measurement block, so it is equivalent to the stated mutual independence.

standard.name: Independent structural noises with separate latent roots
standard.citation: Yang, Yuqin, AmirEmad Ghassami, Mohamed Nafea, Negar Kiyavash, Kun Zhang, and Ilya Shpitser. 2022. ``Causal Discovery in Linear Latent Variable Models Subject to Measurement Error.'' Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35. arXiv:2211.03984.

nl.statement: The covariance of \(H_e\) equals \(\Omega_{H,\mu}\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\).

review.note: Unfolding covariance and latentPart gives exactly Cov(H_e) = Ω_H for every environment.

standard.name: Group-wise stationary confounding
standard.citation: Pfister, Niklas, Sebastian Weichwald, Peter Bühlmann, and Bernhard Schölkopf. 2019. ``Robustifying Independent Component Analysis by Adjusting for Group-Wise Stationary Noise.'' Journal of Machine Learning Research 20(147):1--50. arXiv:1806.01094.

nl.statement: The covariance of \(\eta_e\) equals the same diagonal matrix \(\Omega_{\eta,\mu}\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\).

review.note: Unfolding covariance and measurementPart gives exactly Cov(η_e) = Ω_η for every environment, while CovShiftModel independently pins Ω_η as diagonal.

standard.citation: Yang, Yuqin, AmirEmad Ghassami, Mohamed Nafea, Negar Kiyavash, Kun Zhang, and Ilya Shpitser. 2022. ``Causal Discovery in Linear Latent Variable Models Subject to Measurement Error.'' Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35. arXiv:2211.03984.

nl.statement: Every coordinate of \(\omega_{0,\mu}\) is strictly positive.

review.note: The Lean predicate is exactly strict positivity of every coordinate of ω₀.

standard.citation: Yang, Yuqin, AmirEmad Ghassami, Mohamed Nafea, Negar Kiyavash, Kun Zhang, and Ilya Shpitser. 2022. ``Causal Discovery in Linear Latent Variable Models Subject to Measurement Error.'' Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35. arXiv:2211.03984.

review.note: Matrix.PosDef is the standard positive-definiteness predicate, and the model independently pins Ωη as diagonal.

review.note: The Lean predicate is exactly the cardinality equality |Tμ| = r.

standard.citation: Yang, Yuqin, Saber Salehkaleybar, and Negar Kiyavash. 2024. ``Learning Unknown Intervention Targets in Structural Causal Models from Heterogeneous Data.'' Proceedings of AISTATS, PMLR 238:3187--3195. arXiv:2312.06091.

nl.statement: For every \(j\in T_{\mu}\), there exists \(e\in\{1,\ldots,E\}\) such that \(\lambda_{ej}>0\).

review.note: Fin E indexed through e.succ is exactly the nonbaseline set {1,…,E}, so the quantified target-coverage condition is equivalent in both directions.
Matrix.PosDef on θ.cov 0 states exactly that the baseline covariance Σ₀ is positive definite.

standard.name: Nonsingular Gaussian covariance
standard.citation: Strieder, David, Tobias Freidling, Stefan Haffner, and Mathias Drton. 2021. ``Confidence in Causal Discovery with Linear Causal Models.'' Proceedings of UAI, PMLR 161:1217--1226. arXiv:2106.05694.

nl.statement: The aggregate shift \(\bar Q=\sum_{e=1}^E\Delta_e\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(\bar Q)=r\).

review.note: aggregateShift is exactly the sum of Δₑ over e=1,…,E, and the Lean predicate asserts its rank equals r.
Submodule ≤ is range inclusion, and e.succ ranges exactly over e=1,…,E, yielding precisely range(Δₑ) ⊆ range(Q̄) for every nonbaseline environment.

nl.statement: For every \(e\in\mathcal E\), the generic tuple satisfies \(mI_d\preceq Z_e\preceq MI_d\).

review.note: The two positive-semidefinite difference conditions are respectively equivalent to mI_d ≼ Zₑ and Zₑ ≼ MI_d for every e in 𝓔.

standard.name: Uniform covariance eigenvalue bounds
standard.citation: Lewis, Daniel J. 2022. ``Robust Inference in Models Identified via Heteroskedasticity.'' Review of Economics and Statistics 104(3):510--524.

nl.statement: The generic aggregate difference \(\sum_{e=1}^E(Z_e-Z_0)\) has rank \(r\).

review.note: Unfolding aggregateShift and covarianceShift gives rank(∑ e : Fin E, (ζ.cov e.succ − ζ.cov 0)) = r, exactly the stated aggregate-rank condition.
The quantified Fin E indices map via succ exactly to environments 1 through E, and submodule ≤ is precisely inclusion of each shift's linear range in the aggregate-shift range.

nl.statement: There exist \(T\subseteq\mathcal V\) with \(\lvert T\rvert=r\) and an ordering \(t\) of \(T\) such that \(\operatorname{Cert}(\zeta,T,t)\) holds.

review.note: Finset (Fin d), card r, and Orders encode a size-r subset of the vertex set with an injective exhaustive ordering; the additional Orders conjunct already inside Cert is logically redundant.

standard.citation: Romano, Joseph P., and Azeem M. Shaikh. 2010. ``Inference for the Identified Set in Partially Identified Econometric Models.'' Econometrica 78(1):169--211.

nl.statement: Conditional on \(\theta\), the observations \(Y_{ei}\sim N(0,\Sigma_e)\) are independent over all \(e\in\mathcal E\) and \(1\le i\le n_e\).

review.note: The statement jointly requires independence of every environment-sample variable, measurability, Gaussian pushforward law, zero coordinate means, and second-moment matrix θ.cov e, which is exactly the fixed-θ independent N(0,Σ_e) experiment.

standard.name: Independent multi-sample Gaussian covariance experiment
standard.citation: Lewis, Daniel J. 2022. ``Robust Inference in Models Identified via Heteroskedasticity.'' Review of Economics and Statistics 104(3):510--524.

nl.statement: \(\mathcal M_{d,E,r}=\{\mu_{d,E,r}: B_{\mu}\text{ is acyclic};\ (H_e,\varepsilon_e,\eta_e)\text{ obey the centered Gaussian and independence conditions};\ \operatorname{Cov}(H_e)=\Omega_{H,\mu};\ \operatorname{Cov}(\eta_e)=\Omega_{\eta,\mu};\ \omega_{0,\mu}>0;\ \Omega_{\eta,\mu}\succ0;\ |T_{\mu}|=r;\ \lambda_{ej}=0\text{ off }T_{\mu};\ \lambda_{ej}\ge0\text{ on }T_{\mu};\ \forall j\in T_{\mu}\ \exists e\in\{1,\ldots,E\}:\lambda_{ej}>0\}\).

review.note: After unfolding all member predicates, the structure imposes exactly the paper's acyclicity, centered joint Gaussianity, block independence, stationary covariances, positivity, target cardinality, shift exclusion/nonnegativity, and nonbaseline panel coverage; its dimension and target-size clauses restate global domains.

nl.statement: \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\iff [\,t\text{ orders }T,\ \bar Q_{tt}\succ0,\ \bar Q_{tt}=L_tD_tL_t^{\mathsf T},\ L_t\text{ unit lower triangular},\ D_t\text{ diagonal positive},\ \Lambda_{e,t}=L_t^{-1}P_t\Delta_eP_t^{\mathsf T}L_t^{-\mathsf T}\text{ diagonal and entrywise nonnegative for every }1\le e\le E\,]\), where \(\bar Q=\sum_{e=1}^E\Delta_e\) and \(\bar Q_{tt}=P_t\bar QP_t^{\mathsf T}\).

review.note: After unfolding Orders, aggregateShift, orderedPrincipalBlock, transformedTargetBlock, IsDiagonal, and EntrywiseNonnegative, Lean states exactly the ordered positive LDLᵀ certificate and every nonbaseline transformed block condition.

nl.statement: \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{causal}}(\theta)=\{T\subseteq\mathcal V:|T|=r,\ \exists\mu\in\mathcal M_{d,E,r}\text{ with }T_{\mu}=T\text{ and }\operatorname{Cov}_{\mu}(Y_e)=\Sigma_e\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E\}\).

review.note: Lean quantifies exactly over legal covariance-shift models with target T and all environment covariances equal to θ; under LegalCovShiftModel, covOf is the covariance of the stated centered block-independent observation.
Lean gives exactly the cardinality-r targets admitting an ordering with Cert; the additional Orders conjunct is redundant because Cert already contains it.

nl.statement: Given \(\operatorname{Cert}(\theta,T,t)\), set \(W_t=\bar QP_t^{\mathsf T}\bar Q_{tt}^{-1}\), \(A_t=W_tL_t\), \(U_t=\begin{psmallmatrix}L_t&0\\A_{t,T^c}&I_{d-r}\end{psmallmatrix}\) after placing \(t\) first, and \(B_t=I_d-U_t^{-1}\).  Choose \(0<\tau<\lambda_{\min}(\Sigma_0)/(2(\lVert U_t\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}^2+1))\), set \(R_0=\Sigma_0-\tau U_tU_t^{\mathsf T}-\tau I_d\), and set \(C_t=U_t^{-1}R_0^{1/2}\).  Take \(H_e\sim N(0,I_d)\), baseline structural and measurement covariances \(\tau I_d\), and in environment \(e\) place the increments \(\operatorname{diag}(\Lambda_{e,t})\) on \(t\) and zero increments off \(T\).

review.note: The record realizes every displayed construction, with the explicit slack formula providing a valid canonical choice in the stated interval; baseline positivity is intrinsic to that choice and dimension admissibility is a global domain condition.

nl.statement: Initialize \(S=\varnothing\), \(R_S=\bar Q=\sum_{e=1}^E\Delta_e\), and \(M_{e,S}=\Delta_e\).  A label \(j\notin S\) is admissible when \(q=(R_S)_{jj}>0\), \(m_e=(M_{e,S})_{jj}\ge0\), and \(q(M_{e,S})_{:j}=m_e(R_S)_{:j}\) for every \(1\le e\le E\).  With \(u=(R_S)_{:j}/q\), update \(R_{S\cup\{j\}}=R_S-quu^{\mathsf T}\) and \(M_{e,S\cup\{j\}}=M_{e,S}-m_euu^{\mathsf T}\), memoizing only \(S\cup\{j\}\).

review.note: PivotRun initializes the empty subset with the nonbaseline aggregate and shifts, and its child rule exactly encodes the positivity, proportional-column test, rank-one residual updates, depth-r stopping, and subset-keyed reachable leaves.

For each ordering of that target, the aggregate ordered certificate has unit-lower factor equal to the identity and its transformed second-environment target block contains the diagonal entry \(-1/2\), so \(\operatorname{Cert}\) rejects the true target.  The tuple \(\theta^{\mathrm{split}}\) is generated by a member of \(\mathcal M_{3,2,2}\) with true target set \(\{1,2\}\).  Its first-environment covariance shift has rank one, strictly less than \(r=2\), whereas its aggregate carrier \(\bar Q\) has rank \(r\), and \(\operatorname{Cert}\) accepts the true target in both orders.  Thus signed shifts destroy the nonnegative-diagonal necessity and require strict baseline-variance feasibility in place of nonnegativity, whereas an environment that shifts every target is unnecessary for the aggregate-carrier certificate.

nl.statement:
There is no universal correct-certification envelope determined only by \(c=\lim\delta_n(\theta_n)\).  For any specified Gaussian tangent geometry \(\mathcal G=(k,g_0,\mathcal A)\), where \(X\sim N(g,I_k)\), \(g_0\) has the focal classification, and \(\mathcal A\) is the opposite-classification tangent set, the geometry-indexed focal-certification value is
\[
 \beta^{\star}_{\mathcal G}(\alpha)
 =\sup_{\substack{\phi:\mathbb R^k\to[0,1]\ \mathrm{Borel}\\
                    \sup_{g\in\mathcal A}\mathbb E_g\phi(X)\le\alpha}}
   \mathbb E_{g_0}\phi(X).
\]
The nearest-opposite distance \(c=\inf_{g\in\mathcal A}\lVert g-g_0\rVert_2\) does not determine this value.  Explicitly, for \(k=1\), \(g_0=0\), and opposite sets \(\mathcal A_+=[c,\infty)\) and \(\mathcal A_{\pm}=(-\infty,-c]\cup[c,\infty)\), with \(c>0\),
\[
 \beta^{\star}_{\mathcal G_+}(\alpha)=\Phi(\Phi^{-1}(\alpha)+c),
 \qquad
 \beta^{\star}_{\mathcal G_{\pm}}(\alpha)=2\Phi(t_{c,\alpha})-1
 <\beta^{\star}_{\mathcal G_+}(\alpha),
\]
where \(\Phi\) is the standard-normal distribution function and \(t_{c,\alpha}>0\) is the unique solution of \(\Phi(t-c)-\Phi(-t-c)=\alpha\).  Thus the handle yields an explicit optimization only after the incident tangent geometry is supplied; neither a one-variable \(\beta^{\star}(c)\) nor one classifier attaining it uniformly over all regular sequences is determined by the frozen core.

review.note: After unfolding the geometry, honesty, Gaussian-law, supremum, and nearest-distance definitions, Lean states the same two equal-distance geometries, both exact envelope values, the unique positive threshold equation, and the strict value separation; these witnesses imply the paper's no-scalar-envelope and no-uniform-attaining-rule conclusions.
